title: Observation of Dyakonov-Perel-type magnon spin relaxation in uniaxial antiferromagnetic insulators
authors: Qinwu Gao, Andi Cong, Bokai Liang, Meng Yang, Jingjing Liu, Lang Chen, Shiwei Wu, Ka Shen, Junxue Li
abstract: Long-distance transport of magnon spin currents in antiferromagnetic (AFM) insulators has attracted tremendous attention recently, however, the AFM magnon spin relaxation mechanisms remain elusive. Here, we report that the Dyakonov-Perel-type magnon spin relaxation mechanism governs the spin current transport along the easy axis in two prototypical uniaxial AFM insulators, Cr2O3 and alpha-Fe2O3. First, an over 450% enhancement of the first-harmonic nonlocal signal induced by a magnetic field is observed prior to the spin-flop transition, which can be well-interpreted by our model incorporating Dyakonov-Perel-type magnon spin relaxation. Secondly, we find that the magnon spin diffusion length in both crystals increases with magnetic field and saturates at fields above 0.8 T, consistent with our model. Finally, the temperature dependence of the zero-field magnon spin diffusion length in both AFM insulators can be qualitatively explained through our model. These findings are valuable for the development of low-dissipation antiferromagnetic spintronic devices.
summary: This work investigates magnon spin relaxation in uniaxial AFM insulators using nonlocal transport measurements. The authors successfully identify the Dyakonov-Perel mechanism as the governing relaxation process, explaining field-dependent enhancements in the spin signal and the temperature dependence of the spin diffusion length. These findings are crucial for designing low-dissipation antiferromagnetic spintronic devices.
main_problem: The primary goal is to elucidate the elusive magnon spin relaxation mechanisms governing spin current transport in antiferromagnetic (AFM) insulators.
main_result: The study reports that the Dyakonov-Perel-type mechanism governs spin current transport in $	ext{Cr}_2	ext{O}_3$ and $\alpha	ext{-Fe}_2	ext{O}_3$, evidenced by field-dependent enhancements in the nonlocal signal and saturation of the spin diffusion length.
method: The research combines nonlocal transport measurements (using AC and DC techniques) with theoretical modeling based on the DP relaxation mechanism.
model_or_system: The physical systems are uniaxial AFM insulators ($	ext{Cr}_2	ext{O}_3$ and $\alpha	ext{-Fe}_2	ext{O}_3$). The theoretical framework models magnon spin relaxation using the Dyakonov-Perel analogy, treating magnons as carrying pseudospin.
key_observables: Nonlocal first-harmonic resistance ($R_{1\omega}$), magnon spin diffusion length ($\lambda_s$), and the dependence of these quantities on applied magnetic field ($B_0$) and temperature.
important_parameters: Magnetic field strength (especially relative to the spin-flop transition field $B_{SF}$), temperature, and the characteristic relaxation time ($	au_s$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the spin current propagates along the easy axis and draws an analogy between magnon dynamics and electron spin dynamics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the DP-type relaxation on the Bloch sphere, the measurement setup, and comparisons between different theoretical models (e.g., gap closure vs. DP-model) for the nonlocal resistance.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the context of magnon spin transport, then presents the experimental measurements showing field-dependent anomalies, systematically rules out alternative relaxation mechanisms, and finally confirms the DP-type model by fitting the field and temperature dependencies of the key observables.
why_interesting: The application of the DP mechanism, typically associated with electron spin relaxation, to magnons provides a powerful, transferable theoretical tool for understanding spin dynamics in insulating magnetic systems, which is relevant to quantum spintronics.
